name: Newton
author: E. T. Carter
description: Thin-film interference between two sheets of glass: a warped plate touching a flat one at several points, so Newton rings tighten outward from every contact, bend where the basins meet, and wash into a pale sheen at high order. Four wavelengths each carry a palette pole and beat into shifting spectral fringes, dust motes wear their own tiny ring systems, and the plate breathes so the rings sweep slowly in and out.

params.label: Curvature
params.effect: How strongly the plate is warped; low gives a few broad rings, high packs in many fine ones.

params.label: Coherence
params.effect: Fringe order at which the colours wash out; low is a few coloured rings in a pale field, high keeps fringes crisp far out.

params.label: Breathing
params.effect: How fast the plate breathes and the film ripples; 0 holds the rings still.

params.label: Ripple
params.effect: Soap-film wobble in the gap; 0 is perfect glass rings, high is a restless liquid film.

params.label: Brightness
params.effect: Brightness of the fringes against the dark glass.

params.label: Mouse influence
params.effect: How hard the pointer presses the plates together, adding rings; 0 ignores the mouse.
